title: The Latest SSSOM release (mim-sssom-2026-09-21) still publishes 37 exactMatch rows that main has since removed
body:
This repository's latest release is still `mim-sssom-2026-09-21` ("MIM SSSOM: 1,763 supported mappings", published 2026-09-22). I compared its `ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv` (sha256 `39d81bd6…`, matching the release digest) with `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv` on `main` (1742bfd4, 2,985 rows), keyed on (subject, predicate, object). 37 release rows no longer exist on `main`.

- All 37 are `skos:exactMatch`.
- All 22 subjects still exist on `main`. Each now has a different exact identity, or keeps the old term only as a `broadMatch` parent.
- The rows were removed by #746 (3), #754 (28) and #798 (6).

Examples:
- `MIM:Acridine_Orange`: CHEBI:51739 in the release, CHEBI:87346 on `main`.
- `MIM:Rifamycin`: NCIT:C29406 in the release, CHEBI:26580 on `main`.
- `MIM:Bergenin`: an `exactMatch` to CHEBI:69499 in the release; on `main` CHEBI:69499 is only a `broadMatch` parent.
- `MIM:Lysozyme`: `cas:2650-88-3` in the release. That CAS number fails its check digit (#753). `main` has `kgmicrobe.ingredient:lysozyme`.

Anyone who downloads "Latest" gets identities that `main` has since corrected. I did not check who consumes the release.

Suggested: cut a new reviewed SSSOM release from `main`, or stop marking this one as latest until there is one. Also decide what triggers a release: every merge that changes an identity, or a schedule.
